evidence.claim: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay R$100,000 in collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and physical attacks on journalists.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro é condenado por dano moral coletivo a jornalistas
evidence.excerpt: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay R$100,000 in collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and physical attacks on journalists.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph quoting the judge's reasoning
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire service, and the report quotes the court's reasoning directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's public rhetoric as president and candidate.
contrary_evidence: This is a civil judgment, not a criminal conviction.
The Planalto did not immediately comment in the report.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro gathered diplomats at the Alvorada and repeated unsupported attacks on Brazil's electronic voting system, falsely calling it unauditable and using TV Brasil to broadcast the event.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro chama embaixadores para atacar processo eleitoral; TSE rebate
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro gathered diplomats at the Alvorada and repeated unsupported attacks on Brazil's electronic voting system, falsely calling it unauditable and using TV Brasil to broadcast the event.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent contemporaneous coverage and includes detailed quotations plus TSE rebuttal context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, before the October election.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential conduct; the event was organized and led by Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: Bolsonaro's team later argued it was a government act, not campaign propaganda.
The TSE and observers repeatedly said the electronic system was auditable.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he would respect the October election result only if the vote was 'clean and transparent', maintaining conditional language when asked whether he would accept an adverse result.
evidence.title: No JN, Bolsonaro diz que vai reconhecer resultado das eleições desde que "limpas e transparentes"
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he would respect the October election result only if the vote was 'clean and transparent', maintaining conditional language when asked whether he would accept an adverse result.
evidence.source_locator: Interview quotes in the first half of the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters directly reports Bolsonaro's own public statement in the campaign period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro statement in his capacity as incumbent and candidate.
contrary_evidence: This was a public promise, not proof that he later rejected the result.
He did not yet have the final vote outcome when he said it.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro again raised unsupported fraud suspicions about the electronic voting system, declined to disclose a military report, and repeated claims that the urns were unauditable despite repeated TSE explanations.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro volta a questionar urna eletrônica e diz que análise está sendo feita pelas Forças Armadas
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro again raised unsupported fraud suspicions about the electronic voting system, declined to disclose a military report, and repeated claims that the urns were unauditable despite repeated TSE explanations.
evidence.source_locator: Interview quotes and TSE context in the body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters captures Bolsonaro's repeated public statements and places them against the TSE's prior explanations and election-observer findings.
contrary_evidence: Observers and the TSE said they had found no fraud in Brazil's electronic voting system.
The military review was incomplete or undisclosed at the time of the report.

evidence.claim: Folha reported that Caio Mario Paes de Andrade, Bolsonaro's nominee for Petrobras CEO, did not meet the legal experience requirement because he had not spent the required time in the relevant industry or in comparable senior roles.
evidence.title: Petrobras: indicado para Petrobras não tem a qualificação exigida, dizem minoritários
evidence.excerpt: Folha reported that Caio Mario Paes de Andrade, Bolsonaro's nominee for Petrobras CEO, did not meet the legal experience requirement because he had not spent the required time in the relevant industry or in comparable senior roles.
evidence.source_locator: Passage summarizing the law's experience requirement and Andrade's career background
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The piece cites the legal standard and contrasts it with the nominee's resume; it is a concrete appointment-quality claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's appointment choice through the federal government.
contrary_evidence: The nominee still had to pass corporate-governance review.
This is evidence of questionable qualification, not proof of personal enrichment.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Brazil's securities regulator found it strange that the federal government insisted on nominees to Petrobras' board who had been vetoed by the company's governance process.
evidence.title: CVM estranha insistência de governo sobre conselheiros vetados, dizem fontes
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Brazil's securities regulator found it strange that the federal government insisted on nominees to Petrobras' board who had been vetoed by the company's governance process.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and quoted CVM language
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong independent reporting and the article quotes the regulator's reaction to the nominations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's government because the Union, under his administration, was the controlling shareholder.
contrary_evidence: This is about governance pressure, not a proven personal payoff.
The board process itself still involved formal review mechanisms.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he had warned his relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation related to the family's property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que alertou parentes sobre possível busca e apreensão relacionada a compra de imóveis
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he had warned his relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation related to the family's property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable for contemporaneous quotations; the claim is Bolsonaro's own public reaction to the scrutiny.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro statement; relevant because it shows his response to scrutiny over family finances.
contrary_evidence: This is his own defense, not proof of obstruction.
Warning relatives is not by itself a proven crime.

evidence.claim: Folha reported that Federal Police analysis of Mauro Cid's phone showed suspicious fractional deposits and withdrawals that suggested payments for personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.title: PF sees suspicious transactions in Bolsonaro's office
evidence.excerpt: Folha reported that Federal Police analysis of Mauro Cid's phone showed suspicious fractional deposits and withdrawals that suggested payments for personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and the quotation block summarizing the police findings
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The article is based on police analysis and states the allegation carefully as an ongoing investigation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bolsonaro's close office network and first-family finances, though still under investigation at the time.
contrary_evidence: The report describes suspicions, not a proven criminal conclusion.
The presidential office denied wrongdoing and said the money came from a private account.

evidence.claim: Alexandre de Moraes ordered an investigation into the leak of a police inquiry about suspicious payments for Michelle Bolsonaro's expenses, with reports describing fractional deposits and cash withdrawals linked to family bills.
evidence.title: Moraes determina investigação sobre vazamento de informações envolvendo pagamentos de despesas de Michelle
evidence.excerpt: Alexandre de Moraes ordered an investigation into the leak of a police inquiry about suspicious payments for Michelle Bolsonaro's expenses, with reports describing fractional deposits and cash withdrawals linked to family bills.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and follow-up description of the reported financial movements
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports the court-ordered investigation and the underlying allegation with concrete detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Bolsonaro because the investigation concerns the first family and the presidency's internal network.
contrary_evidence: This source focuses on a leak investigation, not a finding of guilt.
The underlying financial allegation remained under investigation.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro publicly attacked Alexandre de Moraes after the judge authorized a privacy breach in an inquiry involving suspected payments for Michelle Bolsonaro's expenses, demanding the values be disclosed before the election.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro reforça ataques a Moraes por investigação sobre pagamentos de despesas de Michelle
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro publicly attacked Alexandre de Moraes after the judge authorized a privacy breach in an inquiry involving suspected payments for Michelle Bolsonaro's expenses, demanding the values be disclosed before the election.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters story
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters directly captures Bolsonaro's public response to the investigation and the timing relative to the election.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro conduct and rhetoric in response to scrutiny of family finances.
contrary_evidence: This is a political attack on an investigator, but still a quoted public response rather than a formal obstruction order.
The underlying payments remained allegations at the time.

evidence.claim: The Federal Police concluded there were no minimum evidentiary elements showing Bolsonaro committed a crime in the inquiry about possible interference in the corporation.
evidence.title: PF diz que Bolsonaro não cometeu crime em inquérito sobre possível interferência na corporação
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Police concluded there were no minimum evidentiary elements showing Bolsonaro committed a crime in the inquiry about possible interference in the corporation.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs summarizing the PF report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reporting an official investigative conclusion, which is a strong counterpoint even if limited to that specific inquiry.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro, but in a negative sense: this is counterevidence against a stronger obstruction claim.
contrary_evidence: The conclusion is limited to the criminal standard and that specific investigation.
It does not rule out broader unethical behavior outside that inquiry.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he warned relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation tied to allegations about family property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que alertou parentes sobre possivel busca e apreensao relacionada a compra de imoveis
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he warned relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation tied to allegations about family property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted live-stream remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting based on Bolsonaro's own public remarks, with direct attribution but only self-report on the underlying allegation.
evidence.period_fit: direct 2022 conduct and response to scrutiny
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the warning and public framing came from Jair Bolsonaro; the underlying property-purchase allegation remains investigatory and family-linked rather than adjudicated as his personal wrongdoing.
contrary_evidence: Bolsonaro denied irregularities and said 'money current' does not prove cash payments.
The article reports allegations, not a court finding.

evidence.claim: Federal Police analysis of messages on Mauro Cid's phone suggested fractional deposits and withdrawals intended to pay personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.title: Federal Police Sees Suspicious Transactions in Bolsonaro's Office
evidence.excerpt: Federal Police analysis of messages on Mauro Cid's phone suggested fractional deposits and withdrawals intended to pay personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs summarizing the PF analysis and quoted presidential office response
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-style reporting on a police investigation with specific facts, but still an allegation rather than a judicial finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct nexus to Jair Bolsonaro is plausible because the alleged transactions are tied to his office and family, but the source itself stops short of proving his personal order or benefit.
contrary_evidence: The presidential office denied irregularities and said the money came from Bolsonaro's private account.
The article says the matter was under investigation without accusation or confirmation.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro signed decrees naming a new ANA leadership team, including a former ANA director with engineering and water-governance experience, a public-management analyst, and a director with sectoral regulatory experience, for fixed mandates.
evidence.title: Novos diretores(as) e ouvidor-geral da ANA sao nomeados e tomam posse
evidence.publisher: Agencia Nacional de Aguas e Saneamento Basico (ANA)
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro signed decrees naming a new ANA leadership team, including a former ANA director with engineering and water-governance experience, a public-management analyst, and a director with sectoral regulatory experience, for fixed mandates.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official agency notice with named appointees, mandate terms, and professional backgrounds directly tied to Bolsonaro's decrees.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the appointments were signed by Jair Bolsonaro; the source also shows some appointees had prior technical or public-service experience, supporting competence rather than family favoritism.
contrary_evidence: This is one agency and does not establish the whole patronage pattern by itself.
Some appointees were already inside the public sector, so the source supports competence more than novelty.

evidence.claim: Jose Carlos Oliveira, a career INSS public servant, was sworn in as Minister of Work and Previdencia in the presence of Bolsonaro and said he would continue and strengthen existing INSS policies through automation and better service.
evidence.title: Jose Carlos Oliveira e o novo Ministro do Trabalho e Previdencia
evidence.excerpt: Jose Carlos Oliveira, a career INSS public servant, was sworn in as Minister of Work and Previdencia in the presence of Bolsonaro and said he would continue and strengthen existing INSS policies through automation and better service.
evidence.source_locator: headline, lead paragraph, and possession/continuity paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry notice of a sworn-in cabinet appointment with qualifications and policy intentions stated on the record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because Bolsonaro was present and Oliveira assumed office under his government; the source supports a professional rather than purely loyalist appointment, but it does not by itself show broader cabinet quality.
contrary_evidence: The page is an official self-description of continuity and competence, not an independent assessment of performance.
The page was only reachable as a search result snippet in this session, not as a full open page.

The original TSE-filed 2022 program is only indirectly represented here through a secondary summary.
Independent outcome audits for several flagship measures are still thinner than the implementation claims.
